This file contains the exact same code as in `Report.rmd`, but without any explanatory text.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#### Workspace setup ####
set.seed(912)
# List of necessary packages
packages <- c("tidyverse", "knitr", "FrF2")
# Install missing packages
missing_packages <- packages[!(packages %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
install.packages(missing_packages)
# Load packages
lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE)

#### Read data ####
freeze <- read_csv(here::here("freezing_time_data.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-matrix
#| tbl-cap: "Design matrix and observed freezing times from the experiment. A, B, and C represent initial water temperature (+1 = hot), solution density (+1 = high density), and cup material (+1 = glass), with interaction terms (AB, AC, BC, ABC), and freezing times y_1, y_2, and their mean. The longest freezing time occurred with hot water, high density, and a plastic cup; the shortest with room-temperature water, low density, and a glass cup."

# Create a new dataframe named 'matrix' for the full factorial experiment
matrix <- data.frame(
  Run = 1:8,
  A = c(-1, -1, -1, -1, 1, 1, 1, 1), # Factor A: water temperature (-1: RoomTemp, 1: Hot)
  B = c(-1, -1, 1, 1, -1, -1, 1, 1), # Factor B: solution density (-1: NoSugar, 1: Sugar solution)
  C = c(-1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1), # Factor C: cup material (-1: Plastic, 1: Glass)
  y_1 = freeze$time_1, # Freezing time (minutes) - Replication 1
  y_2 = freeze$time_2 # Freezing time (minutes) - Replication 2
)

# Calculate the average of the two replicates within each run
matrix$y_mean <- (freeze$time_1 + freeze$time_2) / 2

# Compute two-factor and three-factor interactions
matrix$AB <- matrix$A * matrix$B
matrix$AC <- matrix$A * matrix$C
matrix$BC <- matrix$B * matrix$C
matrix$ABC <- matrix$A * matrix$B * matrix$C

# Rearrange columns to a conventional factorial design layout
matrix <- matrix[, c("Run", "A", "B", "C", "AB", "AC", "BC", "ABC", "y_1", "y_2", "y_mean")]

# Display the table
kable(matrix)
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-effects
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of estimated main and interaction effects with standard errors, t-values, p-values, and 95% confidence intervals. Effects A, B, and C are statistically significant with p-values < 0.05. All interaction effects are small and not significant."

# Compute pooled variance (each run has 2 reps)
matrix$Var <- ((matrix$y_1 - matrix$y_2)^2) / 2
s2_pooled <- mean(matrix$Var) # Pooled variance estimate
s_pooled <- sqrt(s2_pooled) # Pooled standard deviation

# Compute standard error of effect
SE_effect <- s_pooled / 2

# Compute effects
effects <- colSums(matrix[, c("A", "B", "C", "AB", "AC", "BC", "ABC")] * matrix$y_mean) / 4

# Compute t-values, p-values, and 95% confidence intervals
df <- 8 # Degrees of freedom for t distribution (2 reps × 8 runs)
t_crit <- qt(0.975, df = df) # t critical value for 95% CI

# Create and round final data frame
effects_df <- data.frame(
  Effect = names(effects),
  Estimate = round(effects, 3),
  SE = round(rep(SE_effect, length(effects)), 3),
  t_value = round(effects / SE_effect, 3),
  p_value = round(2 * pt(-abs(effects / SE_effect), df = df), 3),
  CI_lower = round(effects - t_crit * SE_effect, 3),
  CI_upper = round(effects + t_crit * SE_effect, 3)
)


# Display the results
kable(effects_df, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, fig.pos="H", fig.height=2.1, fig.width=4}
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: fig-halfN
#| fig-cap: "Half-normal plot of absolute effects from the freezing experiment. Points farther from the lower-left corner (A, B, C) represent larger and likely significant effects. Interaction effects are clustered near the origin, indicating insignificance."

# Fit linear model with main and interaction effects
freeze_lm <- lm(y_mean ~ A * B * C, data = matrix)

# Define the estimated effects
effects <- c(
  A = 23.125, B = 14.375, C = -15.625,
  AB = -1.875, AC = -1.875, BC = 1.875, ABC = 3.125
)

# Create a data frame and compute half-normal scores
effects_df <- data.frame(
  Effect = names(effects),
  Value = abs(effects) # Use absolute value of effects
) %>%
  arrange(Value) %>% # Sort effects by magnitude
  mutate(
    Rank = 1:n(),
    HalfNormalScore = qnorm((Rank - 0.5) / n()) # Compute expected half-normal quantiles
  )

# Generate the half-normal (Daniel) plot
ggplot(effects_df, aes(x = Value, y = HalfNormalScore, label = Effect)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) + # Plot each effect as a small point

  # Add text labels for all effects except "A"
  geom_text(
    data = subset(effects_df, Effect != "A"),
    vjust = -0.5, size = 2.5
  ) +

  # Add the label for "A" with custom position
  geom_text(
    data = subset(effects_df, Effect == "A"),
    vjust = 1.7, hjust = 1, size = 2.5
  ) +

  # Axis labels
  labs(x = "Absolute Effect", y = "Half-Normal Score") +

  # Minimal theme with custom axis title font size
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8)
  )
```
